{{Short description|American marine biologist and explorer (1928–2011)}}
{{Distinguish|Jean-Marie Loret}}

'''John Loret''' (November 28, 1928 – August 13, 2011) was an American marine biologist and explorer. He was a teacher at Queens College, [[City University of New York]]. He was the director of the "[https://www.smli.org/post/a-house-by-any-other-name  Science Museum of Long Island ]". In the 1980's John lead expeditions into the Mexican jungle looking for Myan temples. I recall that he had mapped parts of Mexico, before Satellite images were available.  He also had a waterfall named after him.  He was a small man in stature, but a very large man in life. A very driven man of excellence that always pushed people to do better.
<ref name="Newsday - 16 August 2011 - Explorer-biologist John Loret dies at 82">{{cite news|url=http://www.newsday.com/long-island/obituaries/explorer-biologist-john-loret-dies-at-82-1.3101682|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411220938/http://www.newsday.com/long-island/obituaries/explorer-biologist-john-loret-dies-at-82-1.3101682|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 11, 2017|title=Explorer-biologist John Loret dies at 82|last=Murphy|first=William|date=16 August 2011|work=[[Newsday]]|access-date=11 April 2017}}</ref>

Loret was born in [[Albany, New York]] in 1928. He served in the [[United States Coast Guard]] from 1946 to 1949.<ref name="Newsday - 16 August 2011 - Explorer-biologist John Loret dies at 82"/>
He studied at the [[New York University]] and was admitted to the degree of [[Doctor of Philosophy]] at the [[University of Connecticut]] in 1974.<ref name="Newsday - 16 August 2011 - Explorer-biologist John Loret dies at 82"/>

John Loret was the President of [[The Explorers Club]] from 1993 to 1996.<ref name=Explorers-Pres-2006>{{cite web|title=About the Club – History – Club presidents, 1905 to present|url=http://www.explorers.org/about/history/presidents/presidents.php|website=The Explorers Club|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060928065244/http://www.explorers.org/about/history/presidents/presidents.php|archivedate=September 28, 2006|url-status=dead}}</ref>
John was one of the Last of the Old Time Explorers, he sailed with [[Thor Heyerdahl]] in 1955 to Easter Island on the Aku-Aku expedition<ref name="NY Times, Explorer and Educator Sounds Warnings on the Environment"
>{{cite news|last=Tusiani|first=Bea|date=17 May 1982|title=Explorer and Educator Sounds Warnings on the Environment|url=https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1992/05/17/759292.html?pageNumber=234|work=[[NY Times]]}}
</ref>


John Loret Expedition Leader<ref name="Expedition Search of the Maya">{{cite web|title=An Environmental Expedition Course in Search of the Maya.|url=https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ199963|website=eric edgov}}</ref>
